latest_release.name: CodeAssist 3.45.0
latest_release.body:
**LAYOUT DESIGNER (NEW)**
- A **design editor for Android XML layouts**: open a layout and switch to **Design** to build the screen visually
- A **palette** of widgets, each tile previewing what it adds. Drag one onto the screen to insert it, or long-press a view and drag it into another parent
- **Instant drop feedback**: a ghost shows where the view will land, and the layout animates into its new shape
- A **property strip** with visual editors for the selected view: text, size, gravity, margin, color and more
- Any property, or an attribute you add yourself, can also be edited in a **dialog**, which applies its changes when it closes
- A **color picker** that leads with the current value, with library colors folded away
- A **component tree** and a compact element list for picking views that are hard to tap
- **Full-screen Design view**, and on a phone **Split** shows the layout itself next to the code, not the designer's chrome
- On a phone the selection's actions (duplicate, delete, select parent) live in the property strip; on a wide screen the panels dock beside the canvas
- Zoom and pan settle smoothly, and tapping outside a panel closes it
- The preview draws the **status bar, clock and gesture handle**, like a real screen
- Your own **custom views are compiled on demand**; one that cannot be shown is replaced by a stand-in instead of breaking the preview
- A scroll view that already has its child refuses a second one, as Android does

**LAYOUT PREVIEW SPEED**
- The **first preview** of a Material layout on a phone is about ten times faster (40 s down to 4 s on our test layout)
- An **edit shows up about twice as fast**, and a view added with a new id no longer forces a slow full relink
- Previews render faster and lighter overall, and the designer no longer parses the layout on the UI thread

**CLAUDE LINK (BETA)**
- **Connect Claude to CodeAssist**: Claude can read, edit, build and test the project you have open, from the new **Connections** page in the assistant
- **Claude Code and Claude Desktop** connect to the desktop app with one copied command
- **Claude on the web or on a phone** connects through a private link: turn on the link, sign in, and add it to Claude as a custom connector
- The link is a secret: keep it to yourself, and **reset it** from the same page if it leaks
- Claude is told how to use CodeAssist, and which tools only read and which ones change things
- **Long tasks keep going**: a build or test run that outlasts one request is handed back as a job Claude can check on
- Screenshots and previews reach Claude as **images**
- The status bar shows **when Claude is connected** and when it is working
- This is a beta: tell us what breaks

**AI ASSISTANT**
- The assistant can now **create modules**, **remove** them, make one module **depend on another**, and **reload the project** after a `module.toml` or build script changes. Before, a module it wrote by hand did not appear until the project was reopened
- It can **run your tests** and read the result of each test
- It can add a dependency to a chosen **scope**, and **remove** one
- On Android the assistant **keeps working when the app is not on screen**, with a notification that says what it is doing and a Stop button
- A long model name no longer squeezes the chat header's buttons

**FASTER ANDROID BUILDS**
- A **clean build** of a Material app on a phone: about 106 s down to about 32 s
- **Changing a string or a layout** and running again: about 15 s down to about 5 s
- **Adding a new resource** no longer renumbers the others or rebuilds every library's `R`
- An edited resource no longer re-merges and recompiles every library's resources
- Linking resources against the Android framework is much faster
- Signing a Run build is faster: the keystore is unlocked once, and the old-style signature is skipped where the device does not need it
- Projects **below minSdk 26** now use the prebuilt libraries too when you Run on your own device
- **31 more libr

detail.readme:
# CodeAssist [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tyron12233/CodeAssist/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/actions) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tyron12233/CodeAssist?display_name=tag&sort=semver)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/tyron12233/CodeAssist)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2)](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW) CodeAssist is an IDE for Android that runs on Android. You can write Kotlin and Java, preview Compose and XML layouts, and build, sign and install APKs on the phone itself, without a computer or a remote build server. A desktop version for Windows and Linux is built from the same code.

## Features - Kotlin and Java editing: completion, auto-import, errors as you type with quick fixes, go to definition/implementation, reformat and optimize imports. - Android XML completion and validation for layouts, manifests and resource files. - Compose `@Preview` functions render next to the code and update as you edit. XML layouts preview too, including your own custom views. - Builds run on the device: aapt2, kotlinc, ecj, D8/R8 and apksigner. Builds are incremental. Output can be a debug APK, or a release APK or App Bundle signed with your own key. - Multi-module projects, build variants, ViewBinding, AIDL, KSP (Room, Hilt) and Firebase's `google-services.json`. - Dependencies from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, and local JAR and AAR files. - Import an existing Gradle project, or export a project as a Gradle project to open in Android Studio. - Git: clone, commit, branch, merge, stash and push. With a GitHub sign-in you can clone private repositories and open pull requests. - An optional AI coding agent that uses your own API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI or OpenRouter). - Plugins can add languages, build steps, tool windows and project templates. C/C++ (NDK) support is a separate plugin. ## Limitations - CodeAssist does not run Gradle. Build scripts are read when a project is imported (dependencies, version catalogs, the common `android {}` options), but Gradle plugins and custom build logic are not executed. - Only the bundled Kotlin compiler plugins are available: Compose, kotlinx.serialization and Parcelize. - Kotlin support is newer than Java support and has more rough edges. - Large projects are slow to index and build on phones with little RAM. If something you need is missing, open an issue. It helps to know what people are trying to build. ## Download - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases): the Android APK, and the desktop builds for Windows and Linux. - [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code) The Play build and the GitHub APK are signed with different keys, so one can't be installed over the other. ## How it works Gradle is too heavy to run on a phone, so CodeAssist keeps its own project model. Each module's build is a graph of tasks with up-to-date checks, much like Gradle's, and the tasks call the Android tools directly instead of going through the Android Gradle Plugin. Changing one file only re-runs the tasks that depend on it. Java analysis uses Eclipse JDT. Kotlin uses the Kotlin compiler's parser with CodeAssist's own analysis on top, so completion doesn't have to start a full compiler session on every keystroke. Symbol indexes for libraries and the Android SDK are stored on disk and read in place, which keeps memory use flat as projects grow. Compose previews don't install anything. The project's compiled code runs in a bytecode interpreter inside the IDE, against the real Compose runtime. More detail is in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), and the full list of documents is in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Building from source You need JDK 17 or newer (CI uses JDK 25). The Android SDK is only needed for the full build. ```sh # Core modules only: plain JVM, no Android SDK needed CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check # Everything, including the Compose UI and the Android app ./gradlew build # Run the desktop IDE ./gradlew :ide-desktop:run # Build the Android app ./gradlew :ide-android:assembleDebug ``` ## Project layout ``` platform/ core services with no IDE-specific knowledge; everything depends on it lang/ the language SPI, indexes, analysis, and the Java/Kotlin/XML backends build-system/ the incremental task engine and the JVM build pipelines run/ running project code on device: interpreter, bytecode VM, AWT/Swing android/ Android support: facets, variants, SDK data, layout preview services/ dependencies, version control, the project store, analytics, the AI agent plugins/ the plugin SPI and the host that loads plugins app/ the Compose UI and the Android, desktop and command-line launchers tools/ test harnesses ``` Gradle project paths are flat (`:lang-kotlin` lives in `lang/lang-kotlin`); `settings.gradle.kts` maps them. [docs/modules.md](docs/modules.md) describes each module. ## Tests and benchmarks Completion quality, editor latency, indexing and build performance are checked against committed baselines by the `regressionTest` tasks. The numbers below are regenerated on each release. | Area | Metric | Result | |---|---|---| | Java completion **quality** | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 75% / 0.88 | | Java completion **latency** (per keystroke) | member access / type ref | **4.3 ms** / 2.8 ms | | Symbol **index** quality | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 90% / 0.95 | | Symbol **index** query | prefix / fuzzy | ~4.4 µs / ~56 ns | Recall is how often the expected item appears in the completion list at all, top-1 how often it is first, and MRR the average of 1/rank. Latency is measured on the maintainer's machine, so treat it as a rough figure. **2359** tests passing across **434** suites · 0 failing · 4 skipped (framework / `CI_CORE_ONLY`). ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach. Before sending a pull request, run `CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check`; it is what CI runs. Plugin authors should start with [docs/writing-plugins.md](docs/writing-plugins.md). For questions and discussion, join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW). ## License CodeAssist is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The plugin SPI modules (`plugin-api`, `plugin-ui-api`, `platform-core`, `vfs-api`, `project-model-api`, `language-api`, `index-api`, `analysis-api` and `build-api`, published under `io.github.tyron12233`) also carry the Classpath exception (see [LICENSE-EXCEPTION](LICENSE-EXCEPTION)), so a plugin compiled against them can use any license.
